scenes.title: 크기 변화도 움직임이다
lines: In the Game Boy version of Kirby’s Dream Land, Kirby briefly flattens on a ledge and springs up round again. What changes when shape moves along with position? We'll compare scaling, squash and stretch, and changes to the outline that scaling alone can't give us. Translation moves an object, rotation turns it, and scaling changes its size. A sword turning toward the camera can look shorter. That change in viewpoint differs from Kirby’s outline flattening. Alongside translation and rotation, a change in size can give motion its character. Try these transformations separately to see what each one does.

scenes.title: 같은 높이로 튀는 두 공
lines: Let's watch a ball hit the floor and bounce back up. Keep the height and timing identical, and change the shape of just one ball. Flatten it on contact, lengthen it as it rises, then let it become round again. On the same path, the second ball looks softer and seems to carry a force. Kirby rises from a flat shape into a small ball on the ledge. A few changed pixels tell us when the ground was touched. This is called squash and stretch. Shape tells us about material and force, even if the object travels the same distance.

scenes.title: 작아지는 대신 모양이 바뀌게
lines: If you only reduce its height, the ball can look as though it has shrunk. Widening it as it compresses helps it appear to contain the same amount of material. We're looking at visible volume. The sprite shows Kirby’s width and height. It gives us no depth measurement behind the screen. Mass in a physics simulation is a separate quantity. Let's put numbers on our example. Our 3D example doubles the width, halves the height and keeps the depth. Multiply the three scale factors: two times one half times one equals one. That transformation preserves volume. In a flat drawing, compare area by multiplying width by height. If both width and depth change in 3D, include both in the product. These numbers help us spot disappearing bulk during a squash; the artistic pose can still vary.

scenes.title: 같은 납작함에도 윤곽은 다르다
lines: Width and height alone may not produce the desired effect. A simple flattened oval looks different from a shape that carries more bulk at its sides. Their width and height can match while their outlines differ. This is easy to see when translating a squashed pixel drawing into a 3D model. On the ledge the bottom edge is flat while some curvature remains above. That profile feels different from a simple oval. In a sprite you can leave extra fullness along the sides. Scaling an entire sphere down won't produce that outline on its own. Compare the scaled shape with one whose sides we sculpted deliberately. Watch their landings and see which retains the fullness of the original body. Cuphead’s mermaid opens her mouth. Her jaw and cheeks change together, unlike stretching the entire picture. Now we're designing the contour as well as the scale.

scenes.title: 원하는 형태로 표면을 바꾸기
lines: You can draw a target contour and deform the original toward it. A 3D surface is built from points called vertices. Keep the same vertices and move them toward their positions in a target shape. This is a blend shape. Mix the starting and target shapes to get a contour that uniform scaling can't produce. Each point needs a corresponding target, so two arbitrary models won't do. Here you can see it in our own example. At zero we have the original; at one, the target. In between the points move between the two. A similar result on a game screen doesn't reveal which technique produced it. We can observe the sequence of Game Boy sprite shapes. Our study shows one way to reproduce them on a mesh. This demonstration shows one way to build that deformation.

scenes.title: 주먹을 키우는 표현과의 차이
lines: Scale changes can serve different purposes. Enlarging the attacking part can emphasize where the force goes. In our demonstration only the fist gets bigger. The goal here is a stronger-looking impact. Our bouncing ball conveyed elasticity, while the enlarged fist emphasizes an attack. Both change scale, but they tell us different things. The hunter extends the sword to sell the attack. Here the path of arm and blade carries the force, unlike the growing fist in our study. Decide what the viewer needs to see, then choose where and how much to change.

scenes.title: 모양으로 물성과 힘을 더하기
lines: If position and timing feel right but the motion lacks character, check the shape too. Compression, the direction of the stretch and the returning contour suggest material and force. Together with translation and rotation, shape can tell us more about the same movement.
